title: Falcons vs. Packers: Three must-know storylines for Thursday's Week 3 prime-time game
description: Can the Packers put a sloppy start behind them? Will Michael Penix Jr.'s 2026 debut spark the Falcons' offense? In advance of Thursday's game between Atlanta and Green Bay, Dan Parr provides three storylines you need to know.
body:
Thursday night’s battle features two teams yearning for a spark to break out of early-season doldrums. The Packers are playing at home for the first time in 2026 after narrowly avoiding an 0-2 start with a comeback win over the Jets in overtime. Meanwhile, the 0-2 Falcons are still searching for some positive vibes after being trounced in their home opener by the Panthers, 34-3.

Green Bay has a chance to make history on Thursday. With a win, the Packers will break the NFL record for consecutive victories in home openers (currently tied at 13 with the 1976-1988 Miami Dolphins). The Falcons have dropped four straight at Lambeau Field, with their last win in Titletown coming back when the team's current president of football, Matt Ryan, was a rookie quarterback (2008).

Yes, we’re still early in the season, but as far as Week 3 games go, the stakes couldn’t be much higher for either club.

Three must-know storylines

1) Can the Packers clean it up? It’s been an uncharacteristically sloppy start for a team with postseason aspirations after making the playoffs in six of the past seven seasons.

Matt LaFleur’s crew leads the league in penalties and penalty yards. It ranks last in rushing yards. Also, Jordan Love has the lowest completion rate of any quarterback with at least 30 pass attempts (52.1%). The only QB over the last 10 seasons with a lower rate in his first two games of a season (min. 70 attempts) was Trevor Lawrence in the first two games of his career (50%, 2021), per NFL Research.

Yikes.

Obviously, the Packers have been playing shorthanded without edge terror Micah Parsons (PUP list) and bell-cow back Josh Jacobs (Commissioner’s Exempt List), but that doesn’t excuse the penalty issues. Green Bay's not getting any better news on the injury front, either, after losing starting right tackle Zach Bako-Bewele (torn patellar tendon) for the season and wideout Jayden Reed to a back ailment in the win over the Jets.

Maybe the Packers are catching the right opponent at the right time. The Falcons have their own health woes, with CB1 A.J. Terrell (groin) joining an ever-growing list of starting defensive players on the sideline. There’s no way to fix everything with a short week to prepare, but playing a cleaner game -- with Love completing 60-plus percent of his throws -- would be a sign of progress for Green Bay.

2) Is Michael Penix Jr. the hero the Falcons need? Penix is set to make his 2026 debut on Thursday, marking his first game back since tearing his left ACL last November. It’s a very welcome development for a team that averaged a league-low eight points and failed to reach the red zone with journeyman Cooper Rush starting the first two contests.

Penix was cleared for full participation in practice about a month ago, so he's had time to gear up for his return to game action. It’s a huge season for the eighth overall pick of the 2024 NFL Draft, with Atlanta's new brass facing a decision on whether to exercise the fifth-year option in his rookie deal next spring. He compiled a record of just 4-8 as a starter in his first two seasons, completing less than 60 percent of his passes and throwing for fewer than 200 yards per game.

Thursday will give Penix a chance to begin rewriting the narrative around his career, and the Packers are only one game removed from giving up 39 points to a Vikings offense that no one is confusing for a juggernaut. Penix might want to avoid falling into his habit of holding on to the ball for too long, though, going against the team with the third-highest pressure rate in the league (45.6%). Atlanta certainly has stockpiled an enviable collection of weapons at the skill positions, with RB Bijan Robinson, WR Drake London and TE Kyle Pitts all capable of performing at an All-Pro level, which leads me to my next point.

3) Will the Falcons utilize their pass catchers? Atlanta’s wide receivers and tight ends have combined for 17 catches, 173 receiving yards and zero touchdowns in 2026, all the fewest among the league’s WR/TE units through Week 2.

The aforementioned Pitts has only one catch for 15 yards, and he’s been targeted just four times. That’s a problem Atlanta offensive coordinator Tommy Rees acknowledged this week, telling reporters he has to do a better job of showcasing Pitts, who signed a contract extension this offseason that made him one of the highest-paid tight ends in the league. Perhaps the quarterback change will help in that regard, but Pitts has just two touchdown catches in the 12 games Penix has started.

Penix has the arm strength to give the offense the downfield passing game it lacked in the first couple weeks. Now it’s up to the coaching staff to exploit a Packers defense that ranks 28th in red-zone TD percentage allowed (85.7%).
author: Dan Parr

title: Giants QB Jaxson Dart to undergo season-ending knee surgery
description: New York Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart is expected to undergo season-ending knee surgery, NFL Network Insiders Ian Rapoport and Mike Garafolo and ESPN's Adam Schefter reported on Wednesday.
body:
New York Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart will undergo season-ending knee surgery, NFL Network Insiders Ian Rapoport and Mike Garafolo and ESPN's Adam Schefter reported on Wednesday.

Dart has been seeking opinions on the injury he suffered during Monday night's 28-6 loss to the Rams, and the good news is that the ACL is intact, per NFL Network.

However, that will not prevent the QB from needing surgery. ESPN added that Dart suffered damage to his left MCL, PCL and meniscus, with the latter being the main issue.

Giants head coach John Harbaugh confirmed on Wednesday afternoon Dart will undergo season-ending surgery. Harbaugh, who did not specify when the surgery would take place, did leave the door open for Dart to return in the postseason. 

The timeline for a meniscus repair is four to six months, Garafolo noted. 

Harbaugh said Jameis Winston will be the Giants starting QB, beginning this week versus the Tennessee Titans. Jake Haener, currently on the practice squad, will serve as New York's backup this week, per Garafolo, but Harbaugh said the team would be adding a quarterback.

Veteran free agent Jimmy Garoppolo is expected to be a candidate to be brought in, Garafolo said. 

Harbaugh said all options are on the table for adding a quarterback, including a trade. 

Dart went down at the end of the Giants' first drive on Monday in Los Angeles. Winston replaced Dart and struggled, going 11 of 27 for 111 yards and an interception.

Initially, there was optimism surrounding Dart's injury, with the QB finishing the game standing on the sideline in street clothes. ESPN's Laura Rutledge reported during the broadcast that Dart actually attempted to get back in the game before the club took his jersey.

Since then, further imaging delivered a much worse reality.

Dart, the No. 25 overall pick in last year's draft, showed flashes of playmaking ability as a rookie but also missed two games due to a concussion. This year, the QB got off to a sensational start in Week 1, picking apart the Dallas Cowboys in an opening-night win. The optimism didn’t last another quarter.

Darts exit thrusts Winston into full-time duty for Harbaugh’s club. The 12-year vet looked bad in relief on Monday, missing layups a QB of his experience should make. The hope is that it was simply a blip, not a sign of things deteriorating for the 32-year-old.

The Giants opened the season with a swell of positivity in Harbaugh’s first season. Now, less than a fortnight into the season, disaster. The longtime NFL coach has a new beast to manage his way through early in his New York tenure.
author: Kevin Patra

title: 2026 NFL Mexico City pregame entertainment announced
description: The NFL announced that acclaimed Música Mexicana artist Majo Aguilar and Oakland-born Blaxicana singer-songwriter MXKA will perform the national anthems of Mexico and the United States prior to the 2026 NFL Mexico City Game
body:
The National Football League today announced that acclaimed Música Mexicana artist Majo Aguilar and Oakland-born Blaxicana singer-songwriter MXKA will perform the national anthems of Mexico and the United States prior to the 2026 NFL Mexico City Game between the Minnesota Vikings and San Francisco 49ers on Sunday, Nov. 22 at 7:20 p.m. CT (8:20 p.m. ET) at Estadio Banorte.

Majo Aguilar will perform the Mexican National Anthem and MXKA will perform the U.S. National Anthem.

One of the leading contemporary voices in Música Mexicana, Majo Aguilar blends mariachi with a modern artistic vision. A three-time Latin GRAMMY® nominee for Best Ranchero/Mariachi Album and a two-time consecutive Premio Lo Nuestro winner for Mexican Music – Female Artist of the Year, she has become a leading figure in the genre's new generation. Her acclaimed Mariachi Mío project helped redefine mariachi through contemporary influences, while performances at Mexico City's Zócalo, Teatro Metropólitan and Canelo Álvarez's boxing match in Riyadh have further elevated her profile. With more than 533 million global streams, Aguilar continues to celebrate Mexican culture and bring the richness of música Mexicana to audiences worldwide.

“I feel very happy to be able to perform the Mexican National Anthem. Mexico is a beautiful country with a rich culture," said Majo Aguilar. "Thank you to the NFL for inviting me to be part of such a special moment and allowing me to represent my country. It fills me with pride to be Mexican.”

MXKA (“MOH-kah”) is an Oakland-born Blaxicana singer-songwriter whose music blends the storytelling and instrumentation of Música Mexicana with the melodic intimacy of contemporary R&B, a sound she calls R&B Tumbados. Born to a mother from Mexico City and a father from Louisiana, she creates bilingual music that reflects her Black, Mexican and American identities. Her breakout single “La Vuelta” marked a major step in her growing career, with her work also earning recognition from Spotify, Billboard, KQED and Remezcla. She has also performed the national anthem as part of Telemundo’s official FIFA World Cup 2026 coverage and continues to expand the boundaries of contemporary Latin music through her unique cross-cultural perspective.

“Getting to sing the U.S. National Anthem in Mexico City, with the 49ers on the field, is a moment that connects so many parts of my story,” said MXKA. “I was born in Oakland, my mom is from CDMX, and as a Blaxicana artist, I’m proud to carry both my Black and Mexican roots onto a stage this big. I’m deeply grateful to the NFL for trusting me with this moment, and I can’t wait to share it with fans from Mexico, the Bay and everywhere in between.”

On Aug. 31, it was announced that The Warning will headline the halftime show of the 2026 NFL Mexico City Game. The Mexico City performance is one of a record seven halftime shows presented by American Express staged across the 2026 International Games, a lineup of musical performances spanning seven countries and four continents, as the league plays its most international games ever in a single season.

“We are excited to showcase two artists in Majo Aguilar and MXKA pregame in Mexico City, each who have rich and significant connections to the country,” said Tim Tubito, NFL senior director, event and game presentation. “Their powerful renditions of the Mexican National Anthem and the U.S. National Anthem under the lights at Estadio Banorte will set the stage for the NFL’s return to Mexico City.”

Both the Mexico and U.S. anthems, along with the full halftime show, will be broadcast live in Mexico on TelevisaUnivision’s Channel 5 and on ESPN.

The league is committed to growing the game at every level across Mexico, engaging fans year-round through partners, programs and initiatives. Further information around the entertainment and fan events surrounding the 2026 NFL Mexico City Game will follow soon.

Tickets for the 2026 NFL Mexico City Game are on sale now at NFL.com/mexicocity.

To stay up to date on all things NFL Mexico and for more on the 2026 NFL Mexico City Game, follow @nflmx on Instagram, X and TikTok.

Sixty-two regular-season NFL games have been played outside the United States, with London, Berlin, Munich, Frankfurt, Madrid, Dublin, São Paulo, Mexico City and Toronto having hosted games to date.

title: Cowboys defense hopes to stay 'disciplined' vs. Lamar Jackson after struggling with mobile QBs
description: The Cowboys head to Brazil this week to face Lamar Jackson and the Ravens in the NFL's first-ever game in Rio de Janeiro. The revamped Dallas D understands it has its hands full attempting to slow Jackson & Co.
body:
The Dallas Cowboys head to Brazil this week to face Lamar Jackson and the Baltimore Ravens in the NFL's first-ever game in Rio de Janeiro. The revamped Dallas defense understands it has its hands full attempting to slow Jackson and Co.

"We all know what it is," Cowboys pass rusher Donovan Ezeiruaku said, via the team's official website. "You guys know. We know as players the type of guy he is. Somebody who can throw the ball but also run the ball at a very high level. It's easier to say than to do, but our job is to go out there and go do. That's what we're tasked with."

Jackson leads the NFL with 10.0 pass yards per attempt through two weeks. The QB hasn’t run a ton -- 11 carries for 74 yards and a touchdown -- but has looked more spry when he has taken off than a year ago.

The Cowboys must key on his scrambling ability after struggling to stop QB runs in the first two weeks against Jaxson Dart (11/54) and Jayden Daniels (7/69). The Cowboys have allowed the most rushing yards to quarterbacks in the NFL (126) on 19 carries (6.6 YPC). That figure would have been even worse had Daniels not exited last Sunday's game at halftime with an elbow injury.

Dallas must make a more concerted effort to slow Jackson.

"Just being disciplined," Cowboys defensive tackle Kenny Clark said. "Communication, just understanding our rush lanes, playing with extension, powering offensive linemen and just restricting those gaps so you can't get through. But the main thing is just staying disciplined and communicating."

The Ravens, missing Zay Flowers due to a hamstring injury, weren’t as explosive in Week 2, but the combination of Jackson and Derrick Henry will always trouble defenses. Despite just five carries in the second half on Sunday, Henry has 212 rush yards and four rush TDs through two games. He’s tied for the NFL lead in TDs, and only Kenneth Walker III (290) has more rush yards.

Slowing both Jackson and Henry in the same game is a monumental task for any defense.

"It is very unique," Ezeiruaku said. "For a guy who's probably bigger than me, playing running back, you've got to take out the legs, that's the only way to stop a guy like that from running the ball. Easier said than done like it is with Lamar, but it'll be a really good challenge."

On paper, it’s a rough matchup for Dallas’ defense, which, through two games, hasn’t shown significant improvement from a year ago under Christian Parker. Too many mental mistakes remain, there is a lack of pass rush, and the tackling is mediocre.

Dallas enters Sunday’s tilt ranked 32nd in third down percent allowed (68%), 30th in rush yards per game allowed (173.5), 29th in yards per game allowed (391.5), 29th in sacks), 24th in yards per play allowed (5.8), 18th in points per game (24.0) and 17th in pass yards per game (218).
author: Kevin Patra

title: NFL Network: Panthers RB Jonathon Brooks to undergo surgery, miss at least six weeks
description: Panthers running back Jonathon Brooks has experienced another bump in the road. Brooks is expected to undergo surgery Wednesday to repair a core muscle injury, which will land him on IR.
body:
Panthers running back Jonathon Brooks has experienced another bump in the road.

Brooks is expected to undergo surgery on Wednesday to repair a core muscle injury, which is expected to keep him out at least six weeks, NFL Network Insider Ian Rapoport reported, per sources.

The Carolina ball-carrier was placed on injured reserve on Wednesday, knocking him out for at least four games. Panthers coach Dave Canales said Brooks is expected to miss six to eight weeks.

Brooks left early in Sunday’s win over the Atlanta Falcons and did not return.

It’s the latest blow for the 2024 second-round pick, who has dealt with a litany of injuries dating back to college. After missing the start of his rookie season while rehabbing a torn ACL, Brooks took just nine carries over three games before tearing the knee ligament again. He missed all of 2025.

Brooks returned this offseason with renewed optimism that he could be the player the Panthers envisioned when they selected him with a second-round pick. In his first two games of the 2026 season, he touched the ball 11 times for 73 yards.

Given the buoyancy the coaching staff had when discussing Brooks this offseason -- noting he finally looked like the player they saw on his college film -- the latest injury is a bummer for the back. It’s a reminder that getting healthy and staying healthy are two different burdens.

The hope is that Brooks can return healthy later in the season and provide some pop out of the backfield. In the meantime, Chuba Hubbard will continue to shoulder the load, with veteran AJ Dillon as the backup.

The Panthers are working out veteran Austin Ekeler, Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 in Houston reported Wednesday. Ekeler, 31, played in two games in 2025 before tearing his Achilles. If healthy, Ekeler could potentially be a pass-catching option alongside Bryce Young.
author: Kevin Patra

title: George Kittle on 2-0 49ers' offense: It's 'a dream come true'
description: The San Francisco 49ers have put up 62 points in two blowout wins to open the season and Brock Purdy has yet to be sacked as Kyle Shanahan's offense is rolling.
body:
Venturing from San Francisco to Australia and back to The Bay, it’s been a blissful two weeks to start the season for George Kittle and the 49ers.

First was a 27-7 blowout of the rival Los Angeles Rams in the NFL’s historic Australian debut.

Next was a walloping of the Miami Dolphins, 35-13.

For Kittle, playing in the current 49ers’ offense is a complete delight.

"I got really lucky," Kittle said Tuesday on The Rich Eisen Show. "I get to play with Trent Williams, right? We got him. Hall of Famer, plays like a Hall of Famer still. Mike Evans, Hall of Famer, plays like a Hall of Famer still. And so just when you add guys like that, it's just so much fun 'cause, I mean, every time we call a play and I know Mike has a chance of getting the ball, I'm like, 'This is so sick.' Brock Purdy's throwing the ball to Mike Evans and I'm blocking for him.

"What a dream come true."

Kittle, a seven-time Pro Bowler, noted that outside of the wide receiver room, highlighted by offseason signee Evans, the 49ers' offense is mostly a collection of familiar talent. And it’s going glowingly thus far.

"I think the biggest thing is that this is essentially like the same offense we've had for quite a while now," said Kittle, who had four receptions for 80 yards and a touchdown against the Dolphins. "It's the same starting O-line as last year. It's the same quarterback, the same fullback, the same running back, the same tight ends. The wide receiver room has changed a little bit. Deebo (Samuel)’s been a part of it before. I think Mike Evans would work in any offense because of how good he is."

With Purdy off to a sensational start, having yet to be sacked and leading the NFL with an 80.4 completion percentage whilst throwing five touchdowns, the 49ers are, indeed, humming.

Kittle stressed a game-by-game approach and outlook, underscoring that their Week 3 tilt against the Arizona Cardinals would be a tough one. At the moment, however, Kittle's smiling wide. It’s a good time to be a 49er.

“The Niners are playing well, feeling good about ourselves right now," he said. "Football’s fun, isn’t it?”
author: Grant Gordon

title: Ex-Ravens RB Jamal Lewis on Derrick Henry's lack of carries in loss: 'Don't make that mistake again'
description: Baltimore Ravens running back Derrick Henry received just five carries in the second half of Sunday's loss to the New Orleans Saints.
body:
A bruising Baltimore Ravens running back of the past is confused by the use, or lack thereof, of a Charm City standout of the present.

In the aftermath of Derrick Henry getting just five carries in the second half of the Ravens’ 24-17 loss to the New Orleans Saints on Sunday, Baltimore’s all-time leading rusher, Jamal Lewis, was blunt in his criticism of the approach.

“He’s a workhorse,” Lewis said on the BMore Football Podcast. “You’re not going to have a workhorse like that for long, so you better use him.”

Henry, 32, finished the Week 2 defeat with 16 carries for 68 yards and a touchdown.

Henry had rushed for 51 yards and a 1-yard touchdown on 11 carries as Baltimore held a 14-6 halftime advantage. In the second half, he was given just five totes and earned 17 yards and the Ravens squandered a lead that was as wide as 11 points in the opening half.

Baltimore getting away from giving Henry the ball has been a curious occurrence at times dating back to John Harbaugh's reign. In the 2025 Ravens’ win-or-go-home Week 18 battle against the Pittsburgh Steelers, for instance, Henry had 15 carries for 112 yards in the first half, but was given the ball just five times in the second half of the 26-24 loss.

It was confusing for many then, and it remains a conundrum now.

“If I only got the ball 10 times in the second half, I was pissed off,” said Lewis, who admitted it was a much different situation when he played than for Henry, who lines up in the backfield with Lamar Jackson, the most prolific rushing quarterback in NFL history.

Lewis still remains the Ravens’ leading rusher with 7,801 yards.

Like Henry, Lewis has a 2,000-yard season to his credit. Unlike Henry, Lewis owns a Super Bowl ring.

If Henry, Jackson and Baltimore are to contend for a Lombardi Trophy, Lewis is of the mind that Ravens first-year offensive coordinator Declan Doyle will need to feed the rock to Henry more often.

In two-plus seasons with Henry playing for the Ravens, Baltimore is 12-3 when the two-time rushing champion has 20-plus carries. It’s 1-0 this year after he rumbled for 144 yards on 24 carries in a 41-23 season-opening win against the Indianapolis Colts.

“Hopefully the offensive coordinator and the head coach learn from the mistake, being that it is early in the season,” Lewis said. “Don’t make that mistake again.”

The Ravens are headed to Brazil this week to take on the Dallas Cowboys, who have given up more rushing yards this season than all but two other teams. It portends to be a prime opportunity for head coach Jesse Minter and his staff to heed Lewis’ advice.
author: Grant Gordon

title: Hall of Famer Adam Vinatieri kicks world record field goal in Swiss Alps
description: Hall of Fame kicker Adam Vinatieri earned a spot in the Guinness World Record book with his latest feat.
body:
Adorned with four Super Bowl victories, three Pro Bowls and more than 2,600 points scored, Adam Vinatieri was basking in the warmth of a Canton, Ohio, summer day back in August.

 Just more than a month later, Vinatieri was bundled up, back to kicking and setting a record.

The Hall of Famer, who played 10 seasons with the New England Patriots and 14 more for the Indianapolis Colts, set a Guinness World Record on Tuesday for kicking the highest field goal in the world, converting from an altitude of 3,454 meters (11,332 feet) above sea level in the Swiss Alps.

The 53-year-old Vinatieri’s kick took place at Jungfraujoch, known as the “Top of Europe,” on snow-covered ground with swirling winds.

“Snow is simply part of my time with the Patriots,” said Vinatieri, who converted plenty of kicks in snowy conditions during his career, including in the 2001 season’s AFC Championship Game against the Raiders. “But kicking a field goal at 3,454 meters is something completely different from anything I've ever done. You feel the altitude with every breath you take, your heart rate is different, your rhythm is different, and no one can really tell you beforehand how it will affect the kick, because no one has done this before. The fact that we were able to set the record under these conditions makes me very proud.”

Vinatieri split the uprights in front of a small, but joyous gathering.

Having made his last official NFL kick on Dec. 1, 2019, for the Colts, Vinatieri’s latest boot was official, according to Guiness.

It also came with him donning a Patriots jersey as part of the Patriots’ countdown to their Nov. 15 game in Munich, against the Detroit Lions.
author: Grant Gordon

title: NFL Network: Giants' Jaxson Dart potentially out for season after testing shows worse knee injury
description: Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart could miss the rest of the season after Tuesday testing showed his knee injury is worse than initially feared, NFL Network Insiders Ian Rapoport and Mike Garafolo and ESPN's Adam Schefter reported.
body:
Jaxson Dart's 2026 season is in jeopardy.

The New York Giants starting quarterback could potentially miss the rest of the season after testing on Tuesday showed his knee injury is worse than initially feared, NFL Network Insiders Ian Rapoport and Mike Garafolo and ESPN's Adam Schefter reported.

Schefter added Dart could undergo season-ending surgery.

“Right now evaluations are ongoing. We haven’t gotten any final decisions yet," Giants head coach John Harbaugh said on Tuesday, minutes after the report broke. "We’ve learned a lot more. I wouldn’t really want to share too much until decisions get made and that takes more than one person. It takes everybody involved. 

"When we know what direction we’re going to have to go … we’ll announce that, but we don’t have that yet. So, I don’t want to get out over our skis on that. Can’t really respond to every report that people make. Got to work on our own timeline here.”

Harbaugh was asked specifically about the report Dart could miss the rest of the season.

“I don’t think I can really comment on any of that right now until we know for sure what’s going to transpire," he said.

Dart suffered the injury -- which, reportedly, was initially believed to be a sprained MCL -- at the end of the Giants' first possession in their 28-6 loss to the Rams on Monday night. Jameis Winston replaced Dart, completing 11 of 27 passes for 111 yards and an interception.

Dart walked off the field under his own power and was taken into the locker room for further evaluation Monday night, which initially produced results that were encouraging enough for Dart to attempt to re-enter the game, ESPN's Laura Rutledge reported during the broadcast.

Harbaugh echoed the optimistic sentiment afterward, telling reporters on Monday that it appeared Dart avoided "the devastating outcome" and landed "in the neighborhood" of an MCL sprain, adding New York would know more after a Tuesday MRI.

Tuesday wasn't as positive, and now the Giants might have to confront a reality they'd hoped to avoid.

Dart's knee injury marks the second instance in which he's been sidelined due to health challenges. He missed two games in 2025 due to a concussion and has attracted attention for his fearless style of play, which has left him susceptible to more hits than the average quarterback.

The hit that caused the injury on Monday night, however, occurred with Dart under duress in the pocket and had nothing to do with his scrambling aggression. Unfortunately, the outcome is too familiar to the Giants, who must shift toward preparing Winston as their starter for the foreseeable future.

Winston started two games in place of Dart in 2025, going 0-2 in one-score losses to Green Bay and Detroit. New York felt confident enough about Winston's capabilities as a veteran backup to reward the 2015 No. 1 overall pick with a two-year, $13 million extension earlier this month, locking down a trusted second option behind Dart.

He'll have a chance to prove the Giants weren't misguided in their faith when New York hosts the Tennessee Titans (0-2) on Sunday.
author: Nick Shook

title: NFL Network: Bears QB Tyson Bagent in concussion protocol; Case Keenum could start Week 3
description: Bears backup QB Tyson Bagent is in concussion protocol, putting his status in question for Chicago's Week 3 game against the Eagles. Veteran Case Keenum could get the start under center.
body:
The Chicago Bears could face a quarterback conundrum on Monday night against the Philadelphia Eagles.

Backup Bears quarterback Tyson Bagent is in concussion protocol, NFL Network Insider Ian Rapoport reported Tuesday, per sources. With Caleb Williams dealing with a hamstring injury that coach Ben Johnson said Monday likely puts him out this week, veteran Case Keenum could be in the starting saddle in prime time.

Bagent entered the game in the fourth quarter of Sunday’s 9-3 loss to Minnesota after Williams exited with the hamstring injury. He completed 5 of 9 passes for 54 yards. On the final play of the game, Vikings' Dallas Turner slammed Bagent to the turf for a sack.

Playing on Monday gives the Bears an extra day to get Bagent through concussion protocol before having to pull the emergency handle in Keenum.

The 38-year-old is in his second season with the Bears, mostly acting as an extra coach in the QB room. Keenum hasn’t thrown a pass or started a regular-season game since 2023 with the Houston Texans. In his 11-year career, he’s started 66 contests -- only four since 2020 -- with a career 62.3 completion percentage, 15,175 yards with 79 TDs and 51 INTs. Best known for the Minneapolis Miracle in 2017, Keenum is a wild card at this stage. Can he perform like a savvy vet who understands defenses, knows when to take his shots, and can manage the offense? Or might he look like an elderly signal-caller meant more for his film prowess than on-field acumen?

If Bagent doesn’t clear protocol by Monday night, we’ll find out.
author: Kevin Patra

title: NFL QB rankings, Week 3: Patrick Mahomes, Dak Prescott, Matthew Stafford heating up
description: Thirty passers are on the move in Nick Shook's QB rankings, with Dak Prescott entering the top five. Check out the updated pecking order, 1-32, heading into Week 3 of the 2026 NFL season.
body:
NOTES:

Up/down arrows illustrate movement from the Week 2 QB Index.
Stream live local and prime-time games on mobile with NFL+ .

TIER 1

Josh Allen can do no wrong, following up a four-touchdown season debut with a five-touchdown showing in Week 2. He has an early lead in the MVP race.
Patrick Mahomes has proven he’s completely back from the knee injury that ended his 2025 season. He fired majestic strikes and moved with the full capability that has defined his brand in the win over the Colts. The fact he’s operating in an offense that now has a legitimate running game is an added bonus.

Next Gen Stats insight (via NFL Pro): Mahomes completed 8 of 9 passes for 133 yards and two TDs against man coverage in Week 1, a contrast to a 2025 campaign in which his 5.0 yards per attempt against man were the second-fewest in the NFL and his five INTs were tied for second-most.

Brock Purdy is another early MVP candidate after lighting up the Rams and Dolphins to start the season, posting a league-best completion percentage of 80.4.
Dak Prescott got back on track in Week 2, dropping an absurd amount of gorgeous dimes on CeeDee Lamb in a 37-20 romp over Washington and reminding the football world of his elite talents (yes, I called him elite and I’m not exaggerating).
Matthew Stafford returned to form after looking rusty in his 2026 debut, torching the Giants by leaning heavily on Davante Adams.
Jared Goff was excellent in the second half of Detroit’s Week 2 loss, a reality that will be lost on most who only check final scores. For the Lions’ sake, hopefully his efforts will produce more wins going forward.

Next Gen Stats insight (via NFL Pro): Goff has the most games with 2+ passing touchdowns and zero interceptions in the NFL since the start of 2024 (18), 2023 (25), 2022 (31) and 2021 (35) — the year he was traded to the Lions.

TIER 2

The Bengals were a bit uneven offensively against Houston’s top-tier defense, but they won with big plays made possible by Joe Burrow’s arm talent, decision-making and willingness to let it rip while under duress. He and the Bengals haven’t been consistently explosive through two weeks, but Burrow deserves credit for going into Houston and leading Cincinnati to a 14-point win.

Next Gen Stats insight (via NFL Pro): Burrow completed all three of his deep passes (20+ air yards) to Ja'Marr Chase for 73 yards and two TDs in Week 2 against the Texans.

It was jarring to watch Baltimore’s offense lose its juice once Derrick Henry disappeared from the game plan in Week 2, and it didn’t reflect well on Lamar Jackson. Yes, he didn’t have WR1 Zay Flowers available, but Jackson’s inability to overcome a surprising change in defensive strategy -- New Orleans decreased its blitz rate in the second half and improved -- and his game-sealing interception dealt a blow to his sparkling reputation for at least one week.

Next Gen Stats insight (via NFL Pro): Jackson used play action on 34.2% of dropbacks against the Saints, completing 6 of his 10 play-action attempts for 101 yards.

Bryce Young stacked another excellent showing on top of his season debut, making throws that wowed viewers and buoyed his standing in the QB Index. The confidence and conviction represents a significant step forward for a quarterback who needs a career year ahead of contract talks.
Trevor Lawrence was incredibly sharp early in Denver, fitting passes into tight windows and pushing the Jaguars offense forward. His dropoff in the second half was disappointing, though, and contributed directly to Jacksonville’s defeat.

TIER 3

Tyler Shough has an obvious clutch gene and unchecked bravery that has already propelled two second-half comebacks this season and powered the Saints to one of the biggest upsets of Week 2. It sure helps that Chris Olave is blossoming, a product of a symbiotic relationship between quarterback and receiver.

Next Gen Stats insight (via NFL Pro): Shough completed 10 of his 13 attempts against the blitz for 113 yards, a career high mark, while also going 17 for 21 for 139 yards and a touchdown when facing four or fewer rushers.

Drew Lock lit up Arizona in his first start in place of the injured Sam Darnold, throwing without fear and reaping the benefits. He steadied the Seahawks’ offense in a situation that could have taken a downward turn with a lesser quarterback.

Next Gen Stats insight (via NFL Pro): Lock completed 7 of 11 downfield pass attempts (10+ air yards) for 175 yards in Week 2 against the Cardinals, the second-most of his career, along with two touchdowns.

Jalen Hurts tossed a couple of interceptions against the Titans, but he also pushed the Eagles to victory with his late-game heroics. With A.J. Brown no longer in the mix in Philly, Hurts’ rapport with DeVonta Smith is among the most enjoyable developments of the early portion of 2026.
C.J. Stroud has played well at times in the first two weeks, but he hasn’t yet strung together a complete performance.

Next Gen Stats insight (via NFL Pro): Through two weeks, Stroud leads the league in dropbacks (104) and pass attempts (93); only 10.8% of his pass attempts have been thrown at or behind the line of scrimmage, the second lowest rate in the league.

Jayden Daniels played really well in the first half of Washington’s Week 2 loss and likely would have kept the game close to the very end had he not suffered a dislocated left elbow on the final play of the second quarter. It’s a massively disappointing development for both the Commanders and fans of electrifying quarterback play.
Brian Flores’ Vikings defense got after Caleb Williams, whose fast-and-loose playing style burned him when he attempted an off-balance throw on the run that resulted in an interception. Williams still had his moments, but he couldn’t overcome the elements or Minnesota's aggression, and his hamstring injury was an awful way to end his day. We’ll all hope Williams can return near full strength before long because he’s so fun to watch.

TIER 4

Jordan Love was thrown into the rain at MetLife Stadium in Week 2 and, unsurprisingly, he struggled. He did manage to lead a comeback victory with an offense that lacks any semblance of a running game, though. He’ll need to improve before long, or else he’ll continue to hover around the Dalton Line.
Daniel Jones did his best to keep the Colts in a thrilling Sunday night contest and nearly threw them to victory.

Next Gen Stats insight (via NFL Pro): Jones used play action on 51.5% of his dropbacks vs. the Chiefs, his second-highest rate in a game in his career and was effective when doing so, completing 14 of his 16 attempts for 159 yards and a touchdown, his second-most yards on play action passes in a game in his career. 

Kirk Cousins has been tremendously fun to watch, especially for fans of grizzled veterans who might be getting their final chance to play meaningful football before Father Time arrives. Cousins’ play against the Chargers was heroic at times, and he’s done a great job of quieting the conversation regarding rookie Fernando Mendoza’s eventual rise to the top job.

Next Gen Stats insight (via NFL Pro): Cousins joined Tom Brady (2021 & 2015) and Peyton Manning (2014) as the only quarterbacks age 38 or older with at least three touchdown passes in each of his team's first two games of a season.

Drake Maye played better against the Steelers than the 20-3 final score suggested, but the Patriots have a problem with finishing drives. Maye still isn’t close to the elite quarterback he was in 2025.

TIER 5

Justin Herbert isn’t the main reason the Chargers are 0-2. He’s made plenty of excellent throws, but he also isn’t helping Los Angeles in key moments when taking unnecessary risks that result in turnovers.

Next Gen Stats insight (via NFL Pro): Herbert has gone 0-for-7 with two INTs on tight-window throws this season (less than one yard of separation), while attempting those throws at a 13.0% clip, a mark just below the NFL average (14.3%).

Geno Smith’s solid start carried over into Week 2 for a portion of the contest, but the weather didn’t help his efforts in a disappointing loss.
Bo Nix and the Broncos still have a problem with starting slowly, and Nix continues to vacillate between a quarterback who can make incredible throws and commit maddening mistakes.

Next Gen Stats insight (via NFL Pro): Nix completed 16 of 17 passes against four or fewer rushers for 205 yards and a TD in Week 2 against the Jaguars, tied for the second-highest completion percentage when not facing the blitz by any quarterback since the start of last season (min. 10 attempts).

Jaxson Dart’s encouraging start to 2026 was interrupted by a knee injury that wiped out the rest of his season, throwing the Giants into a depressing and familiar scenario from which they thought they’d graduated.

TIER 6

Cam Ward and the Titans were much better offensively in Week 2. They gave the Eagles a four-quarter battle most didn’t expect to see. Ward appears to be gaining confidence in Brian Daboll’s offense and has regained some of his playmaking ability that drove optimism after his rookie season, although there’s still plenty of room to grow. 
It was nice to see Deshaun Watson produce competent play on a Sunday. It wasn’t great by any means, nor was it pretty, but Watson keyed a second-half comeback that saw the Browns outscore the Buccaneers 17-3 to finish the game, including a 55-yard catch-and-run touchdown for rookie Denzel Boston (his second in as many weeks) and a third-down completion to tight end Blake Whiteheart for the game-winning score. That’s exponentially better than anything I’ve written about Watson in about two years, which is worthy of a bump.

Next Gen Stats insight (via NFL Pro): Watson is the first starting QB to lead a fourth-quarter comeback to snap a 6+ game personal losing streak since Justin Fields (2025).

Jacoby Brissett played better against the Seahawks than his stat line suggested in the first half by leaning heavily on Trey McBride. For two quarters, it appeared as if Brissett might go toe-to-toe with Drew Lock. That optimism faded in a lopsided second half in which Brissett couldn’t overcome the suffocating Seattle defense.

Next Gen Stats insight (via NFL Pro): Brissett was under pressure on 41.9% of dropbacks in Week 2 against the Seahawks, completing 4 of 11 passes for 9 yards with an INT under pressure, and 13 of 17 for 86 yards and a TD from a clean pocket.

We have real reason to be concerned about Tampa Bay’s offense, a scheme in which Baker Mayfield simply appears uncomfortable and uncertain. I’m not sure there’s a quick fix to this issue, either. A frantic, skittish Mayfield isn’t going to be capable of overcoming an offense that lacks identity, rhythm and confidence.

TIER 7

Malik Willis is trying his best to lead an offense that simply doesn’t take care of the details and carries one of the lowest ceilings in the NFL. It’s not necessarily his fault, but it’s clear he’s not quite the quarterback who can carry an undermanned team to victory at this stage in his career.
Aaron Rodgers’ age was painfully obvious in New England on Sunday. His offensive line struggled to protect him, his receivers didn’t help him and he didn’t look like he enjoyed his job very much. Somehow, an offense with more freedom to be aggressive has produced worse results, and at 42 years old, it looks like Rodgers isn’t capable of overcoming these challenges right now.

Next Gen Stats insight (via NFL Pro): Rodgers finished with 187 passing yards, 0 touchdowns and 1 INT -- his fifth straight start with one passing TD or fewer, tied for the second-longest such streak of his career.

Carson Wentz’s performance was entirely forgettable in a rainy 9-3 victory in Chicago. We’ll see if Kyler Murray’s return can get the offense back on track.
Cooper Rush has been the worst quarterback in the NFL through two weeks, but thankfully, Michael Penix Jr. is returning to the lineup this week. We’ll see if his style of play fits better than that of Rush, who wasn’t helped much by an underperforming offensive line.

title: Drew Brees says he reached out to Broncos about comeback prior to AFC Championship Game
description: Hall of Fame QB Drew Brees says he reached out to the Broncos about a potential comeback prior to last season's AFC Championship Game.
body:
Ahead of last week’s tilt between the Broncos and Chiefs, ESPN reported that the Broncos reached out to Drew Brees prior to last season's AFC Championship Game about a potential return.

The news caused a kerfuffle in Denver, with head coach Sean Payton saying last week that he’d never heard of Brees’ comeback consideration.

During Monday’s episode of the “Let’s Go” podcast on SiriusXM, co-host Jim Gray asked Brees how close he was to actually giving it a shot to return.

“Well, I'd say this. So my wrist and my shoulder, I don't throw with my right side anymore,” he said. “I mean, I could throw it 10 yards and it's with a lot of pain, you know? So that's definitely not gonna get the job done. Now, my mind, my body, everything else feels great, but my right wrist, right shoulder wouldn't allow it to happen. But did I think about it? Absolutely, 1,000 percent. I would've loved to come back and play for the Broncos in the AFC Championship Game, get my coach and a bunch of the other guys that I know in that organization, the Penner family, to the Super Bowl. Would've loved it.”

The physical inability was one reason Brees couldn’t make a comeback. The other is that he remains on the New Orleans Saints reserve/retired list.

Brees said it was during his Pro Football Hall of Fame door knock that he truly thought about the possibility of returning. The HOF QB noted that he initiated a text to then-Broncos assistants Pete Carmichael and Joe Lombardi.

“Here's the story. So I get the knock (from the Hall of Fame), I get the knock literally on Monday, January 19. It was the day after the Divisional Round, where the news had come out that Bo Nix had hurt his foot, he was gonna be out,” Brees said. “So Jim Porter, who's the president of the Hall of Fame, we're there, we're having this moment. Dan Fouts is telling me I'm in the Hall of Fame. And I look at Jim Porter and said, ‘Well, I guess this means I can't go back and play for the Broncos this week.’ And he goes, ‘Actually, you can do whatever you want.’ He said, ‘Voting's already been done, you're in, you can do whatever you want.’

“And so I'm telling you when I say I like flipped the switch, I flipped the switch. Immediately texted Pete Carmichael and Joe Lombardi, my OC and quarterback coach with the Saints, they were with the Broncos. I said, ‘You guys need me this week?’ I said, ‘I might be able to be ready.’ And they're like, ‘Are you serious? We'll go down and tell Sean right now.’ I said, ‘Wait, let me get up tomorrow. Let me give this thing a go.’ So I got up the next morning and I gave it a go. I had my 13-year-old son catching balls for me in the backyard. And man, it just was not happening with the right side. Left side, inside the 20 I would have been lethal. At least could have gotten them in and out of the right plays. But no, it wasn't going to happen.”

Added Brees: “That was the end of it, yeah. Texted them back and said, ‘Ah, look, I'll be there for moral support.’”

The moral support went for naught on that day. The Broncos started backup Jarrett Stidham in Nix's stead and lost, 10-7, to the Patriots in rough weather conditions.
author: Kevin Patra

title: Aaron Glenn defends late-game decisions made in Jets' loss to Packers
description: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn is standing by decisions he made late in his team's Week 2 loss to the Packers.
body:
The New York Jets undoubtedly played better in their first two games of the 2026 season than they did in Aaron Glenn’s first campaign as head coach. However, some questionable decisions by Glenn in the Week 2 collapse against the Green Bay Packers linger.

Glenn's first surprising choice came late in the fourth quarter of a tied game, when he declined to call a timeout to give his offense one last shot with the ball before overtime. On Monday, Glenn doubled down on defending the decision.

“When we have the punter at the logo, we don’t want to put ourselves in a situation where we get our guys in a backed-up situation,” Glenn said, via the New York Daily News. “I know we are talking about getting our offense going in that situation. But the thing is, they also had two timeouts.

“I just felt like it was the right decision to do at that point. And we actually wanted to play for overtime when it came to that.”

Perhaps nothing would have come of a last possession in regulation, but I believe Glenn missed an opportunity to see if something could pop that would tilt the game in the Jets' favor. Crazier things have happened for teams with roughly a minute left and a timeout. The choice to play conservative even surprised Packers coach Matt LaFleur.

“Oh yeah, I was really confused by that,” LaFleur said after Sunday’s game. “That’s why we called the timeout and tried a Hail Mary.”

Glenn's other debatable call came with the decision to take the ball first in overtime. With the rules allowing for both teams to possess the ball, clubs have become more likely to want the ball second. Glenn said after the loss that he wanted the ball to control the clock during the 10-minute overtime. Instead, a series of miscues pushed the Jets back and into a quick three-and-out. From there, the Packers had a relatively easy drive to win the game.

On Monday, Glenn was asked if he regretted any of his decisions. He said the game didn’t come down to one or two plays.

“There are always going to be decisions in that case,” Glenn said. “I think every coach has that – that’s offense, defense and special teams. I think when the clock got to 11 seconds, I could have easily called a timeout there and forced a punt. We actually ended up getting a sack on the play, so there are other plays in that game that determined the outcome of that game.”

The reality for Glenn is that, in his position, coaching under the microscope in New York and coming off a horrific first season, his decisions will be picked apart after a loss, especially after a 10-point fourth-quarter lead was withered away.
author: Kevin Patra

title: Matthew Stafford, Davante Adams dominate Giants in Rams' blowout win
description: Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford tossed four touchdown passes, including two to receiver Davante Adams, in Los Angeles' blowout Monday night win over the Giants.
body:
Aaron Donald returned to the field on Monday night, and so did the Los Angeles Rams’ offense, which was absent in Week 1. The two felt intertwined in the 28-6 blowout victory over the New York Giants at SoFi Stadium.

Monday marked Donald's first game back since he retired after the 2023 season.

“I was so juiced. He came running out of the tunnel and I couldn't control myself,” Matthew Stafford said of Donald’s return. “I was freaking fired up. I'm sure y'all were in there. The fans were happy to see him back and we all were, too. Just the human being, the player, all of it combined. What he brings to our team and to our locker room is unmatched. And really to the city, which I thought was amazing. I thought it was a great reception for him tonight, well-deserved.”

The juiced Stafford went out and ripped apart the banged-up Giants secondary, whipping four touchdowns on 22 of 31 passes for 327 yards. New York pressured Stafford on just 15.2% of his dropbacks, the fourth-lowest rate he has faced in a game as a Ram (since 2021), per Next Gen Stats. When kept clean, he completed 20 of 27 attempts for 302 yards, including all four touchdowns and his lone interception -- which was a heat-check deep shot in the second quarter.

Despite not having All-Pro receiver Puka Nacua, Stafford moved the ball at will, feeding Davante Adams. The reigning MVP hit Adams with 8 passes for 195 yards and two TDs. The rest of the Rams offense combined for 132 receiving yards.

“He’s wide receiver one to me. He ain't a two,” head coach Sean McVay said of Adams. “He was special and it showed all night. That's what he's consistently done and I'm really happy for him. I thought he made some great plays, but you could see there's a lot of trust that he and Matthew have. They were able to get a lot of work together this offseason, and it's only going to continue to build. I was really happy for him. He did his thing tonight.”

According to Opta Stats, the most yards by a QB-receiver duo 33 or older in a game in NFL history is 289 by Steve Young and Jerry Rice on Dec. 18, 1995. Stafford and Adams came in No. 2 on Monday with 195.

A week after struggling to move the ball consistently against the 49ers in Australia, the Rams moved unimpeded through the Big Blue defense, gobbling up 481 yards and 23 first downs. They converted 5 of 9 third downs, and went 3-of-3 in the red zone. Outside of two turnovers in the second quarter, L.A. did whatever it wanted.  

With Donald returning, the Rams' D played with a little more fire and rattled backup quarterback Jameis Winston, who was thrust into action after Jaxson Dart’s first-drive injury. Playing a more physical brand of defense than a week ago, L.A. gave up just 182 total yards, 11 first downs and two field goals.

Donald noted that the speed of the game didn't feel like too much after two years off.

“The game really wasn’t as fast as I thought,”  he said. “It was more of me calming myself down, overrunning stuff or just my feet not being in the ground how they supposed to be, not trusting my eyes, little stuff like that. But playing the game, when I held out in ’17, ’18 it was the same way when I came back, it took a couple games to get going. It’s a little different. I ain’t played in two years, so I gotta watch the film, see what I did good, see what I did wrong, and just clean it up.”

In his return, Donald had three tackles, including one for loss, and one quarterback pressure on 18 pass rushes, tied for his career low, per Next Gen Stats.

After last week’s dismal performance against San Francisco, the Rams got back on track at home. McVay even took a shot at himself for the Australia travel plans, which were roundly panned after the blowout loss.

“Sometimes you win, sometimes you learn,” he said. “Sometimes you have a dumbass coach that makes travel plans that put you in a bad spot. So there you go. That's a dropped mic.”
author: Kevin Patra

title: Giants-Rams on 'Monday Night Football': What We Learned from Los Angeles' 28-6 win
description: The Los Angeles Rams cruised to their first win of the season in prime time against the New York Giants.
body:
Home sweet, home for Rams. Basking in the comfortable confines of SoFi Stadium, the Rams returned home from a wayward Australian adventure and returned to the form so many thought would be seen. Matthew Stafford looked like the MVP from a season ago, Davante Adams looked like the game-tilting wide receiver he was for years and the Los Angeles defense, with Aaron Donald at the center of it all, was sterling. As the Giants sputtered with Jaxson Dart lost to a knee injury, the Rams overcame a couple of turnovers and won handily. More than a week removed from falling flat in their opener in the outback against the 49ers, the Rams handled their business and were impressive. Stafford, rebounding from a zero-touchdown Week 1, proved that was an aberration with 327 passing yards and four touchdown passes. That he did so without an injured Puka Nacua was all the more impressive. Adams was simply wonderful in the No. 1 WR role, hauling in a pair of touchdowns and nearly 200 yards, while the two-headed running game of Kyren Williams and Blake Corum also got the job done (164 combined rushing yards). In a game that felt like a blowout despite the Rams leading by only two scores throughout most of the night, L.A. racked up 481 yards. It wasn’t perfect. There were turnovers and too many missed opportunities, but the Rams got right on Monday, happy to be home, feeling, looking and playing like themselves.
Monday nightmare for Giants. Seven snaps into the game, Jaxson Dart was savagely sandwiched by the Rams’ pass rush and left grasping his left knee. That was it for Dart on Monday. Before he was ruled out, though, Dart was joined as being questionable to return by wide receiver Malik Nabers. Fortunately, Nabers returned to play after dinging up his shoulder. Dart never got back in, and Andrew Thomas (groin) and Brian Burns (ankle) were injured late in the game. It was a nightmare of an evening for the Giants. It was reported Dart tried to return to action and general manager Joe Schoen said he’d be OK, eschewing long-term concerns for the time being. Meanwhile, the Giants offense was a struggle bus with Jameis Winston at the helm. The running game went nowhere, either. Cam Skattebo was the team’s leading rusher with just 36 yards on 12 carries and was curiously replaced by Najee Harris for two runs inside the 10-yard line late in the first half. The biggest takeaway in this one is that the Giants’ offense is absolutely lost without Dart, and considering his injury history, that puts New York in a precarious spot.  
Donald makes long-awaited return. It had been 981 days since Aaron Donald last played a game -- a wild-card playoff loss against the Detroit Lions. He made a much-ado return Monday. Highlighted by stopping Najee Harris on a third down tackle for loss in the second quarter, Donald contributed three tackles. Perhaps more importantly as head coach Sean McVay said after halftime, he was energizing the Rams defense and Los Angeles was outstanding. Jaxson Dart and Jameis Winston were constantly harassed (each facing 58%-plus pressure rates), and New York's running game went nowhere, held to 52 yards. Once upon a time before Myles Garrett was acquired via trade and Donald unretired, the Rams trading with the Chiefs for Trent McDuffie was their big offseason splash. McDuffie was excellent, recording his first interception with his new team and piling up four pass breakups, allowing no catches on five targets. This was a banner homecoming for Donald and a suffocating performance from the D. 
Davante’s still got it. Puka Nacua was inactive with a hip injury and the Rams’ lack of receiving depth was exposed. Fortunately, Davante Adams let everyone know he’s still got plenty left in the tank, piling up eight receptions on 10 targets for 195 yards and two touchdowns. The catches and yards were tops for his time with the Rams, but underscored that the 33-year-old can still take over a game if need be. And L.A. needed him. Second-year tight end Terrance Ferguson shrugged off some bad drops and finished with six catches for 54 yards and a TD, but his contributions largely came after the game had long been settled. Beyond that, nobody else had more than two catches. Adams was a force, even with Stafford dialed in him. When Adams hauled in an 11-yard fade for six in the third quarter, it wasn’t just vintage Adams, but it looked like a called shot, an inevitable six points that everyone could see coming and simply couldn’t be stopped. 
Big blues on both sides. On the scoreboard, it looked like the Giants’ defense was keeping them in the game. More so it was a Matthew Stafford interception and a Kyren Williams lost fumble on consecutive offensive plays in the second quarter that did the trick. Sure, the NYG D played its part in those, but Rams mistakes let the Giants hang around. In the first half, New York mustered just two QB pressures of Stafford, but somehow only trailed, 14-3. With Jaxson Dart injuring his knee, the Giants collectively seemed to take a punch to the gut, all their wind gone as the game felt like a one-sided affair no matter how close the score was. L.A. totaled 481 net yards on 60 plays (8.01 yards per play). Stafford was pressured on just 15.2% of his dropbacks by game’s end. A week after a Sunday night win over the rival Cowboys made the Giants the talk of the town, they’re leaving the West Coast battered, bruised and beaten in lopsided fashion. They’ll need to mend up, and shore up some issues on both sides of the ball.

Next Gen Stats Insight for Giants-Rams (via NFL Pro): Giants rookie right guard Francis Mauigoa held Aaron Donald to zero QB pressures on 11 matchups. Donald had one total QB pressure, three tackles and a run stuff on 32 snaps in his first game since the 2023 season.

NFL Research: Davante Adams’ 11-yard touchdown catch was the 95th of his career (including playoffs) of 20 yards or fewer, which tied Antonio Gates for second all time. Only Jerry Rice (112) has more.
author: Grant Gordon

title: Rams QB Matthew Stafford moves into sixth all time in touchdown passes
description: Matthew Stafford’s Hall of Fame résumé continues to build and build. Stafford’s latest accomplishment came on Monday when the Los Angeles Rams quarterback threw three touchdowns to move into sixth place all time in NFL history.
body:
Matthew Stafford’s résumé for Hall of Fame enshrinement continues to build and build.

Stafford’s latest accomplishment came Monday when the Los Angeles Rams quarterback threw four touchdowns in a 28-6 win over the New York Giants, with the third score moving him into sixth place all time in NFL history.

Davante Adams caught Stafford’s 426th career touchdown pass, an 11-yarder in the third quarter, to propel Stafford past Philip Rivers (425). He had 427 by the end of the evening. 

“It’s a humbling feeling,” Stafford told ESPN’s Lisa Salters after the game.

Aside from being a historic night for Stafford, it was also a massive rebound performance after he went without a touchdown toss in the Rams’ season-opening loss to the San Francisco 49ers. Stafford, who led the NFL with 46 touchdown passes last season, didn’t go a game without a TD throw in 2025. Now he’s bounced back from his atypical showing in fine fashion.

The 38-year-old very much resides in rarefied air.

The reigning AP NFL MVP has fewer touchdowns than only Tom Brady (first; 649 touchdown passes), Drew Brees (second; 571), Peyton Manning (third; 539), Aaron Rodgers (fourth; 528), and Brett Favre (fifth; 508).

"I have so much respect for the people that played this game before me and am such a big fan of those guys," Stafford told Salters. "So, just to be in that same breath as those guys is a cool feeling for me.”

Stafford's first two TD passes Monday were to Adams and Kyren Williams, with the 10-yarder to Williams standing as his 143rd with the Rams. That put him into second all time in Rams history, moving him ahead of Jim Everett (142). Stafford, in six years with the Rams, now trails only Roman Gabriel (154) for most TD passes in club chronicle. He added his fourth touchdown throw of the game -- and 145th overall for L.A. -- late to tight end Terrance Ferguson.

If Stafford is to catch Favre and/or become just the sixth NFL player to reach 500 TD passes, that would mean playing beyond the 2026 campaign.

For now, however, Stafford has climbed another rung up the all-time ladder, continuing to defy Father Time and pen an argument for a spot in Canton, in the process.

title: Rams WR Puka Nacua (hip) inactive for Monday's game vs. Giants
description: The Rams will be without another star on "Monday Night Football." Puka Nacua is officially inactive for Los Angeles' prime-time game against the Giants.
body:
The Rams will be without another star on Monday Night Football.

Puka Nacua is officially inactive for Los Angeles' prime-time game against the Giants.

The wide receiver popped up on the injury report with what was labeled as a hip issue Friday, missing that practice and the team's Saturday session before receiving a questionable designation. Head coach Sean McVay described Nacua's injury as groin soreness, telling reporters it was not associated with the psoas issue that caused the 25-year-old to miss some time during the preseason.

Regardless of where exactly Nacua is hurting, he's unable to partake in an important game for the Rams as they look to avoid an 0-2 hole to start a season they entered with realistic Super Bowl aspirations.

Although Nacua was not his typically explosive self in Los Angeles' season opener against the 49ers, collecting five catches for 74 yards, he was the only Rams pass catcher to get anything going in the 27-7 loss. His yardage total was nearly half of Matthew Stafford's 155 through the air, and a sizable chunk of it came on a 41-yard connection before the game got out of hand.

His absence is a massive blow for Stafford as the reigning Most Valuable Player looks to get back on track, especially considering wideout Jordan Whittington will also miss the contest due to a quad injury.

Davante Adams is likely in line for a ton of targets and will be supplemented by other receivers such as Konata Mumpfield, Xavier Smith and Tutu Atwell. The Rams also roster a diverse tight end corps led by Tyler Higbee and Terrance Ferguson, and running backs Kyren Williams and Blake Corum are capable of contributing in the passing game, too.

Just a couple weeks into the season, the Rams are already juggling a couple injuries to big names. Along with Nacua being unable to go Monday, Los Angeles will be without Myles Garrett for at least four games after the star pass rusher underwent knee surgery and was placed on injured reserve.

There remains an impressive array of stars in L.A., but McVay's crew is certainly dealing with some difficulties in the early going.

They'll look to overcome them to move to 1-1 when they kick off against the Giants (1-0) on Monday at 8:15 p.m. ET.
author: Bobby Kownack

title: TE Zach Ertz reuniting with Eagles, signing to Philadelphia's practice squad
description: Philadelphia is bringing back one of its best. The Eagles are signing tight end Zach Ertz to the practice squad, ESPN's Adam Schefter reported Monday.
body:
Philadelphia is bringing back one of its best.

The Eagles are signing tight end Zach Ertz to the practice squad, ESPN's Adam Schefter reported Monday.

Ertz, who is coming off a torn ACL suffered while playing for the Commanders last season, began his career as a 2013 second-round draft pick by the Eagles. He racked up 579 receptions, 6,267 yards and 38 touchdowns for Philly over a stretch of eight-plus seasons that included three Pro Bowl campaigns and a Super Bowl victory.

He was traded during the 2021 campaign to the Cardinals, for whom he played through 2023, and then spent a pair of seasons in Washington. He currently sits at 8,592 receiving yards and 57 TDs on 825 career catches.

There had been rumblings that a reunion for Ertz and the Eagles might be on the table, and recent injuries in the tight end room likely made the decision a little easier. Dallas Goedert suffered a sprained MCL on Sunday and will miss some time, while rookie Eli Stowers is currently on injured reserve with a hamstring injury. 

Thus, Ertz is coming back to the practice squad, healthy and with a very real chance to make an impact for the Eagles.

He also has an opportunity to make some franchise history in a hurry, as the 35-year-old returns only 11 receptions shy of the Eagles' all-time catch record currently held by Harold Carmichael (589). 

Ertz is sure to hear the cheers from the Philly faithful assuming he jumps to the active roster and sees the field, and he'll receive yet another ovation should he end up stamping his name in the record books.
author: Bobby Kownack

title: Falcons name Michael Penix Jr. starting quarterback for Week 3 game vs. Packers
description: Michael Penix Jr. will start at quarterback for the Atlanta Falcons in their Week 3 game against the Green Bay Packers, the team announced.
body:
After 10 long months, Michael Penix Jr. is ready for live NFL action.

Penix will start at quarterback for the Atlanta Falcons in their Week 3 game against the Green Bay Packers on Thursday night, the team announced on Monday.

Penix will be making his first start since suffering a season-ending knee injury last November.

He was officially a full participant in Monday's estimated practice report.

Cooper Rush started Atlanta's first two games of the 2026 season, both losses, in place of the sidelined Penix and Tua Tagovailoa, who has been dealing with an oblique injury.

Falcons coach Kevin Stefanski said earlier Monday that he had no update on who his Week 3 starter would be but had an idea where Atlanta was going. In the end, the Falcons are going back to their 2024 first-round pick.

Penix's road back to the field lasted a little longer than expected. After tearing knee ligaments in November and undergoing surgery, Penix was not cleared to fully participate in practice until Aug. 22. Tagovailoa, who was signed in the offseason for the veteran minimum, was named the Week 1 starter over the still-ramping Penix but was sidelined due to an oblique injury suffered during practice that week.

In came Rush, who through two weeks has struggled, to put it mildly. The 32-year-old journeyman completed 56.4% of his passes for 229 yards and a league-high four interceptions in Atlanta's first two games, which it lost by a combined score of 54-16. Rush was benched in the second half of Sunday's blowout loss to Carolina in favor of undrafted rookie Jack Strand, who fared no better.

In Penix, Atlanta hopes to have its first glimpse of a legitimate starting QB leading Stefanski's offense in 2026. Before suffering his season-ending injury, the southpaw was having a solid campaign in his first full year as starter, completing 60.1% of his passes for 1,982 yards, nine touchdowns and three picks. He finished the year with a league-best 1.1 INT percentage.

The Falcons could surely use Penix's sturdy production to get off the mat on a short week. At 0-2, Atlanta will be traveling to face the Packers in their home opener at a hostile Lambeau Field.

Atlanta is no stranger to a left-handed quarterback stunning the Green Bay faithful in prime time (see: Mike Vick in the 2002 Wild Card Round). We'll see if Penix can deliver a similar performance on Thursday Night Football.
author: Jeremy Bergman

title: J.J. McCarthy, Mac Jones, Jimmy Garoppolo and 4 other QBs who could help teams in need
body: The NFL season is only two weeks old, and yet six teams have already dealt with injuries to their starting quarterbacks. The Falcons were already without Michael Penix Jr. because of his recovery from an ACL injury when Tua Tagovailoa went down with a back injury just days before the opener. In Week 1, the Seahawks lost Sam Darnold to a glute injury and Vikings starter Kyler Murray suffered a concussion. Week 2 was even worse: The Commanders lost Jayden Daniels to another dislocated elbow (the same one he dislocated last season), the Bears watched Caleb Williams get carted off with a hamstring injury and then placed backup Tyler Bagent in the concussion protocol, and the Giants saw Jaxson Dart go down with a knee injury that is expected to end his season. The spate of early injuries to quarterbacks has reinforced the value of experienced (and reliable) backups. The teams that have them have remained competitive; Seattle and Minnesota are both 2-0 with respective backups Drew Lock and Carson Wentz filling in. But the teams that lack a solid No. 2 or any real depth at the position have paid a price. Just look at Atlanta, where third-stringer Cooper Rush was benched during a blowout loss to the Panthers after throwing his fourth pick of the season. He was replaced by Jack Strand -- who promptly threw a pick-six. There's good news in store for a few teams. Penix will start for the Falcons on Thursday night, and Tagovailoa is back to fully participating in practice. Darnold is expected to return to practice in some capacity this week for the Seahawks, and Murray has been cleared from the concussion protocol in Minnesota. But that leaves three teams who could be in search of reinforcement. Case Keenum is the only other quarterback on the Bears' active roster and, although he has 66 starts in his 14-year NFL career, he hasn't played a regular-season snap since December 2023.  For Washington, it remains unclear how much time Daniels might miss. X-rays of Daniels' elbow were negative for any fractures, but coach Dan Quinn declined to provide any details about the MRI results. Daniels will not start Sunday against the Seahawks, but how long he'll be out thereafter is unknown. In the meantime, the Commanders will turn to Marcus Mariota, just as they have the past two seasons when Daniels has dealt with injuries. The difference this time around: Washington doesn't have an experienced third-string QB like it had with Josh Johnson last year. The team's current No. 3 is seventh-round rookie Athan Kaliakmanis, a young player who showed some promise in the preseason but is still quite green. The Giants are in an even trickier position. Dart's prognosis is much worse than what was originally expected. Jameis Winston is expected to take over as the starter, but he's the only other quarterback on the Giants' active roster. Jake Haener, a fourth-round pick by the Saints in 2023, is on the practice squad. So who might be available to help? Finding a quality backup quarterback at this point in the season is difficult, but there are several veterans and young QBs who could serve as extra insurance, if not more, for teams in need. From potential trade candidates to street free agents and practice squad players, here are some players who may be under consideration, either now or after the next prominent starter goes down. Mac Jones The sixth-year quarterback has seemingly found his groove with San Francisco as Brock Purdy's backup. After a standout rookie season with the Patriots in which he was named a Pro Bowl alternate, Jones cycled through multiple play callers and quickly regressed. He was traded to Jacksonville in 2024 and started seven games in relief of Trevor Lawrence. But it wasn't until he signed a two-year deal with the 49ers in 2025 that he really showed his worth as a reliable backup. He went 5-3 as a fill-in starter, recording a 69.6 completion percentage, averaging 7.4 yards per attempt and compiling a 97.4 passer rating -- all career bests. San Francisco may want to hold on to him to spell Purdy, but it could also get a decent return from a desperate team for a player who is set to be a free agent after this season. Jimmy Garoppolo The 12-year veteran and two-time Super Bowl winner reportedly considered retirement in the offseason but ultimately decided to keep his options open in the NFL as a free agent. Garoppolo, 34,  hasn't had any real playing time since the 2024 season, when he started the Rams' regular-season finale against the Seahawks, and he hasn't had any consistent playing time since the start of the 2023 season with the Raiders. But he does have a 43-21 record as a starter, to go with a 67.4 career completion percentage and 97.6 passer rating. Josh Johnson Johnson, 40, is in his 19th season of professional football and is still going as a member of the Bengals' practice squad. He is the ultimate journeyman, playing for a record 14 NFL teams. Johnson was Washington's third-string quarterback last season until Daniels went down and he became the backup and then the starter late in the season when Mariota suffered a quad injury. His familiarity with offensive coordinator David Blough and Washington's other quarterbacks could make him a viable option if the Commanders seek outside reinforcement. But Johnson also has deep ties to Giants coach John Harbaugh (and his brother, Chargers coach Jim). Johnson had three stints with the Ravens when Harbaugh was their coach, totaling seven games (one start) and completing 69.8 percent of his passes for 321 passing yards, two TDs, a pick, and a 97.1 passer rating. Will Levis Levis signed to the Jets' practice squad Tuesday, so should the Giants be interested in adding him to their active roster, he'd have a pretty easy move. But would they? The 2023 second-round pick by the Titans showed some promise when he took over for Ryan Tannehill as a rookie. But injuries and poor performances derailed his tenure in Tennessee. He was benched late in the 2024 season, when Giants quarterbacks coach Brian Callahan was Tennessee's head coach. Levis missed all of 2025 because of a shoulder injury and was released last month after losing the backup job to Mitchell Trubisky. Anthony Richardson Richardson never developed into the franchise quarterback the Colts hoped he'd be when they drafted him with the fourth pick in 2023. Injuries, performance issues and general readiness questions after he tapped out for a play during a narrow loss to the Texans in 2024 put him on the outs with the organization. He lost his starting job to Daniel Jones, requested a trade, and is now in the final year of his rookie contract (the Colts declined his fifth-year option). If Richardson is viewed as more of a developmental project, then a team in need of immediate help may be unlikely to trade for him. But never say never. J.J. McCarthy The same context holds for McCarthy, the Vikings' 2024 first-round pick. McCarthy missed the entirety of his rookie season because of a torn meniscus and was sidelined for seven games last season because of injuries. McCarthy fell to third string this season after the team signed Murray to start and re-signed Wentz as his backup. McCarthy has started only 10 games and has more interceptions (12) than touchdowns (11). But he's well liked in the Harbaugh family. Jim Harbaugh once lauded McCarthy as the greatest quarterback in Michigan history. Brandon Allen The 10-year veteran has spent more than four seasons with Callahan: three in Cincinnati, when Callahan was the Bengals' offensive coordinator; another in Tennessee, when Callahan was head coach; and this offseason with the Giants. Allen was among the roster cuts late last month. This article originally appeared in The Athletic.
